description: Phase A (KFT completion), cross-repo. Un-404 the trainer's real output endpoints — the KFT §6 training-telemetry stream, the §5.3 export, and the §8 registry registration — turning today's stubbed/404 surfaces into a live, subscribable stream. These endpoints only come alive when an orchestrator-side KCB finetune CLIENT replaces `Runner::Stub` (discover -> invoke -> subscribe to the §6 stream -> issue `invoke:finetune` grants per §7): the trainer's stream dials that runtime. agora's half is standing the endpoints up as real, subscribable surfaces and proving them with an in-repo KCB client that drives the four-verb dance the orchestrator will run. Cross-repo per ROADMAP Phase A: the orchestrator `90-finetune-client` and `pinakes:90-finetune-provider` land the runtime dialed at deploy time. agora gates on `make check`; the trainer gates on `make check-trainer`.

userStories.title: The §6 training-telemetry stream goes live and subscribable
userStories.description: Turn the KFT §6 training-telemetry from a stub/404 into a live stream over the `/invoke` request (KCB §4 subscribe), one event per training step in monotonic order, content-addressed by `job + step` so redelivery is idempotent, closed by the terminal event carrying the minted finetuned-model id + weight/export asset ids (trainer/README.md §'Admission, engines & telemetry').
acceptanceCriteria: `/invoke` streams real KFT §6 telemetry (one idempotent, content-addressed event per step, terminal event carrying the minted model + asset ids) rather than returning a stub/404 — driven by the recorded-run adapter where no GPU is present (never a fabricated loss curve).
A subscriber (KCB §4 subscribe) receives the ordered event sequence to the terminal event; a test asserts monotonic ordering and idempotent redelivery; `make check-trainer` green.

userStories.title: Un-404 the §5.3 export and §8 registry registration
userStories.description: Make the §5.3 export matrix (weights + each requested export as KMI assets with lineage) and the §8 discovery-registry registration of the minted model entity live, replacing the 404s. Output-egress enforcement at registration (§5.4/FT-A) must refuse a `local-only`-inheriting model a cross-boundary registration (`egress-output`).
acceptanceCriteria: The §5.3 export endpoint returns the real export matrix (KMI assets carrying `media:derived_from`/`media:variant_of` lineage) and the §8 registration surface registers the minted model entity, both replacing prior 404s.

Registration enforces the §5.4/FT-A output-egress rule — a `local-only`-inheriting model is refused cross-boundary registration (`egress-output`), an in-tier one admits — proven by a test; `make check-trainer` green.

userStories.title: An in-repo KCB finetune client drives the four-verb dance end to end
userStories.description: Prove the live endpoints with an in-repo KCB client that runs discover -> invoke -> subscribe -> issue `invoke:finetune` grant — the same dance the orchestrator's `Runner::Stub` replacement (cross-repo `90-finetune-client`) will run at deploy time. This is the agora-side standing proof; the production client is another repo's work.
acceptanceCriteria: A test-scoped KCB finetune client discovers the trainer, invokes a schema-valid job, subscribes to the live §6 stream to the terminal event, and carries an `invoke:finetune` grant token with a `X-Agora-Budget-Units` ceiling (§7) — end to end against the live endpoints, no stub.

The test documents itself as the agora-side stand-in for the orchestrator's `Runner::Stub` replacement (cross-repo `90-finetune-client`), which dials `pinakes:90-finetune-provider` + this trainer at runtime; `make check` green.
